<!-- hive-mind-solve-repository-mode -->

## Objective

Address every open issue listed below in [link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer) with a **single pull request**.

This issue was generated automatically by `/solve https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` (repository mode). Native sub-issues and the complete closing-reference block below jointly define the required scope.

## Scope

- Open issues found in the repository: 10
- Issues requested in this single pull request: 10
- Issues selected for native sub-issue attachment: 10
- GitHub sub-issue limit per parent issue: 100

## Issues to address

- [ ] #3 Detect passport machine-readable zones (ICAO 9303 MRZ): real passport data leaked — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #4 Detect passport numbers without explicit labels (Russian domestic/international and country formats) — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #5 Detect travel booking data: PNR/booking references, e-ticket and visa numbers — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #6 Detect dates of birth in natural language and loose labels — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #7 Identity masking transformation: keep 2+2 characters with *** and fully redact values shorter than 5 — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #8 Allow explicitly fake identity data (specimens, synthetic numbers, reviewed allowlist) but never by context words — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #9 Session JSONL sanitization fails with ERR_LIMIT and redacts JSON structure (tool names, ids) — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #10 Missing credential formats found in competitor test suites: .netrc, NuGet, WordPress keys/salts, PuTTY v3 — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #11 National identifiers without short labels: NHS, RRN, codice fiscale, NRIC, PESEL, personnummer, SA ID, TFN, SIN, SNILS, INN — opened 2026-10-08
- [ ] #12 Detect national-format phone numbers after messenger labels (WhatsApp, Zalo) and in Russian prose — opened 2026-10-08

## Requirements

1. Read every issue listed above (including its comments) and fully implement what it asks for.
2. Do all of the work in this single pull request. Do not defer any listed issue to a follow-up pull request.
3. The pull request description **must** close this issue and **every** issue listed above, so that merging the pull request closes all of them at once.
4. GitHub requires the full closing syntax for each issue: one keyword per issue. `Fixes #1, #2` only closes `#1`. Use the block below verbatim (plus `Fixes #<this issue>` for this issue).
5. If an issue turns out to be already resolved or not reproducible, say so explicitly in the pull request description — but still keep its closing reference so it is closed on merge.

## Required closing references in the pull request description

```
Fixes #3
Fixes #4
Fixes #5
Fixes #6
Fixes #7
Fixes #8
Fixes #9
Fixes #10
Fixes #11
Fixes #12
```
